headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection and data leakage: Claude Code’s filesystem/MCP access can feed LangGraph workflows that may treat its outputs as authoritative.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code reads and writes repo files and can use MCP; LangGraph consumes developer-defined tools and application-defined files. That creates a plausible shared-channel injection path if Claude Code writes attacker-controlled content that LangGraph later parses as instructions. The pathway is not proven by docs alone, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF Claude Code writes content into a workspace that LangGraph later reads as prompts or tool arguments
IF LangGraph nodes parse file contents or tool outputs as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Add a provenance tag to every file passed from Claude Code to LangGraph
Require LangGraph nodes to treat file content as data unless explicitly marked
Disable MCP for Claude Code in shared workspaces
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd; LangGraph can read application-defined files and send data to model providers. In a shared workspace, sensitive code or secrets can flow from Claude Code into LangGraph’s model calls. The profiles do not prove a default shared workspace, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF LangGraph nodes forward file contents or graph state to model providers
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Redact secrets before LangGraph model calls
Restrict LangGraph inputs to minimal structured state
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately after a shared run
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and execute shells. Claude Code also modifies git state, while LangGraph can coordinate multiple nodes over persistent shared state. If they target the same repo or checkpointer-backed workflow, concurrent writes can conflict or overwrite each other. The profiles show overlap but not a guaranteed lock, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or application state
IF no external locking or optimistic concurrency control is enabled
mitigations: Assign disjoint file paths per agent
Pause one agent while the other commits or writes state
Enable locking around shared resources
Review and merge git changes manually before continuing
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can produce code, patches, or file edits that LangGraph may ingest as graph state or tool inputs. LangGraph’s orchestration model can then act on those outputs across nodes. Because the profiles do not show a verification gate between them, a mistaken or malicious Claude Code output can cascade into downstream actions, but the blast radius is not proven irreversible.
conditions: IF LangGraph consumes Claude Code outputs as authoritative inputs
IF downstream nodes execute actions without independent validation
mitigations: Insert a human review step before execution
Require schema validation on Claude Code outputs
Have LangGraph re-derive critical facts from primary sources
Limit downstream nodes to read-only dry runs first
requires-engineering: add verification and rollback checkpoints

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code explicitly handles git credentials and shell environment data, while LangGraph handles application-defined graph state and model-provider API keys. A compliance issue exists if regulated data is placed into the shared workflow, but the profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch by default. I therefore keep this low and cite both because the risk arises from their combined handling of sensitive operational data.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are stored in the shared repo or graph state
IF retention or logging settings differ between the two agents' backends
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Review logging and retention settings for both agents
Store secrets in a dedicated secret manager
Limit graph state to non-sensitive identifiers
requires-engineering: document and enforce a common compliance policy
